Auto-redispatch infra-classed failures (W2.10)
description:
Every infra failure today (stale_execution recovery kills, disk-full silent
deaths, provider truncation) required the OPERATOR to notice and PATCH the task
back to IN_PROGRESS by hand. The failure taxonomy already distinguishes these
from real work failures — the system must retry them itself.

## Scope
1. In taskit-backend's dag_executor, after a task lands FAILED, when
   metadata.last_failure_type is an INFRA class (stale_execution, plus
   agent_execution_failure whose reason is the "did not emit ODIN-STATUS /
   truncated / terminated silently" signature), auto-redispatch: same assignee,
   same model (reuse the existing rework-continuity path from #119), capped at
   2 auto-retries per task (metadata counter), with a status_update comment
   naming the failure class and attempt number.
2. Real failures (agent reported FAILED in ODIN-STATUS, reflection FAIL) are
   NEVER auto-retried — those need judgment.
3. Tests: infra-classed failure → one auto-redispatch with continuity; cap
   respected; explicit agent-reported FAILED untouched.

## Acceptance
- Backend tests green including the new ones (attach output).
- Metadata trail shows attempt counter + failure class per auto-retry.

## Working protocol
- odin runs you on an isolated task branch inside a worktree — do NOT create or
  switch branches; edit and git commit in your working directory.
- Attach proof for every acceptance criterion as task comments.
- Never use git stash. Never edit files outside your worktree.

title: Executor prunes task worktree on DONE (W2.11)
description:
Task worktrees (each ~0.1-1GB with node_modules/venvs) accumulate until spec
finalization; today they filled the disk to 100% and took the whole loop down
(backend API bounced, three running tasks died). The operator pruned by hand.

## Scope
1. When a task transitions to DONE, the backend removes its worktree
   (`git worktree remove --force`) and clears metadata.worktree_path — the task
   branch preserves all work. Failures to remove must not block the transition
   (log + comment instead).
2. REVIEW/TESTING/FAILED worktrees are kept (inspection/rework need them).
3. Tests: DONE transition removes the worktree and keeps the branch; removal
   error does not block the transition.

## Acceptance
- Backend tests green including the new ones (attach output).

## Working protocol
- odin runs you on an isolated task branch inside a worktree — do NOT create or
  switch branches; edit and git commit in your working directory.
- Attach proof for every acceptance criterion as task comments.
- Never use git stash. Never edit files outside your worktree.
